look_here_first: TUMBLEGRASS (long treated as Schedonnardus paniculatus) has a DISTINCTIVE architecture: a low tuft with long, often stiff curved flowering axis and several long, very slender, widely diverging one-sided racemes. On a mature raceme, spikelets sit in TWO ROWS along one side of the axis. Look at the whole branch pattern FIRST; then confirm that unilateral spikelet arrangement and membranous ligule. Old dry heads may detach and tumble.

New Texas photos show true lateral branch and attached small spikelets at finger scale, actual outer blade–sheath transition, basal shoots and wild aboveground flowering tuft. True inner membranous ligule, scaled glume/lemma, roots remain missing. FIELD_READY_PHOTO_GAPS.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Tumblegrass long divergent one-sided racemes are not the densely packed panicle of Lindheimer, nor the short narrow contracted panicle of nimblewill. Sideoats grama bears MANY short pendent lateral spikes along a flowering axis rather than a few long thin stiff racemes. Purple lovegrass has a diffuse branching cloud with spikelets dispersed on very fine branches, not distinctive straight unilateral racemes.

what_to_photograph_for_confirmation: Full rooted low tuft showing long flowering culm and several widely diverging racemes.
Close photograph down ONE mature raceme showing sessile spikelets arranged in two rows on its one side.
Leaf blade showing spiral twisting or white margins with ruler.
Membranous ligule and a dissected one-flowered spikelet with a millimeter scale.
Mature detached tumblegrass seedhead and intact attached head to teach what tumbles.
morphology_keys.crew_identification_guardrails: The long widely spreading flowering racemes are photographable; their microscopic one-sided spikelet arrangement and detachment are not proven by the current photograph.

field_photo_quickcheck.heading: Tumblegrass: look for long spreading racemes
steps: START with the physically archived Matt Lavin photograph: trace the long slender divergent branches arising from a curved central flowering axis, rather than mistaking each branch for an independent flowering stem.

ON A FRESH BRANCH inspect one side of the branch axis: the narrow spikelets are held appressed along one side (secund / unilateral), generally one fertile floret each. The existing photo shows the branch architecture, but its resolution is not proof of counted florets.

LOOK AT THE BLADE–SHEATH JUNCTION with a 1-mm ruler and 10–20× magnification. Under the Schedonnardus treatment Kew describes an ECILIATE MEMBRANOUS ligule (no fringe of long marginal hairs). Do not place a ligule arrow on the overview photo.

CHECK a mature intact 3–4 mm spikelet with a 1-mm ruler: identify two glumes and the single fertile lemma. Source morphology describes a narrow laterally compressed spikelet; the current images do not prove those measurements.

COMPARE the curved axis, alternate spreading lateral branches and tightly aligned spikelets with any superficial windmill-grass lookalike. One-sided aligned sessile spikelets, not just a windmill silhouette, are the confirmation target.
KEEP FIELD_READY_PHOTO_GAPS until a real source-verified same-plant Texas branch macro, ligule and dissected spikelet are archived and reviewed.

In new gallery panel 4, observe actual tiny units appressed to one side of the lateral flowering branch (finger is NOT a 1-mm ruler); panel 5 shows a potted basal bunch with roots underground, panel 6 shows outer leaf/sheath junction without isolated true ligule, panel 7 shows flowering wild Spring Branch plants in habitat.
field_photo_quickcheck.field_rule: Curved flowering axis + long widely spreading one-sided slender branches + appressed unilateral spikelets; confirm an eciliate membrane ligule and single-flowered spikelet at scale.
field_photo_quickcheck.warning: 2026-10-27 new pixel-inspected source JPEGS document a close unilateral spikelet branch and true outer sheath junction. No sub-mm free ligule, actual fibrous root origin, calibrated separated glumes/lemmas or specimen voucher has been established. Individual NC images are conditioned on actual noncommercial reuse.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 01 · LOOK HERE FIRST — CURVED AXIS, LONG SPREADING BRANCHES
field_id_short_tiles.short: Low perennial tuft; stiff curved central flowering axis carries several long, widely divergent, slender lateral racemes.
field_id_short_tiles.details: The real Matt Lavin images show long narrow branches arising along one curved axis, not independent stems. Regional sources report roughly 3–13 branches in Texas and 5–10 in a Montana guide; the count varies. Photograph the rooted crown and complete head with a centimeter scale. The mature head may detach and tumble, so a loose head is not proof of its rooted parent.
field_id_short_tiles.status: REAL SOURCE FLOWERING ARCHITECTURE — NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO SAME ROOTED PLANT

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 02 · LIGULE, COLLAR AND GROWTH FORM
field_id_short_tiles.short: Perennial bunchgrass without obvious rhizomes; true ligule an eciliate membrane, about 1–4 mm in regional descriptions.
field_id_short_tiles.details: At the same flowering plant open the blade–sheath junction; photograph the free papery ligule with a 1-mm ruler and distinguish it from blade-edge hairs. Texas Silveus describes an approximately 3-mm membrane, while Montana gives ~1–1.5 mm. Leaves are narrow and may spiral as they dry. No existing gallery image proves the ligule, roots, or measured leaf margin.
field_id_short_tiles.status: PUBLISHED VEGETATIVE TRAITS — NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO TRUE LIGULE/CROWN

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 03 · ONE-FLOWERED SPIKELETS — INSPECT THE BRANCH FACE
field_id_short_tiles.short: One-flowered, sessile spikelets usually about 3–4 mm in modern Montana/Kew descriptions; older Texas treatment allows ~3–6 mm.
field_id_short_tiles.details: Use a 10–20× view of a mature attached raceme and a 1-mm scale; identify each spikelet insertion, its attachment side and one floret. Kew/GrassBase and the historic Texas treatment describe a unilateral/one-sided arrangement, but an Arizona Extension page also describes alternating spikelets on opposite sides. This wording conflict requires a specimen-backed image before a precise row-orientation arrow or categorical crew shortcut. The current branch photos do not resolve the rows.
field_id_short_tiles.status: SOURCE WORDING CONFLICT — NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO RACHIS INSERTIONS BOTH FACES

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 04 · SEPARATE GLUMES, THREE-VEINED LEMMA AND AWNLET
field_id_short_tiles.short: Two narrow 1-veined glumes; Texas treatment gives lower ~2–4 mm, upper ~2.5–6 mm; three-veined fertile lemma ~3–5 mm.
field_id_short_tiles.details: Older Texas Silveus reports short glume awn tips variably present; Kew GrassBase emphasizes narrow acuminate glumes and an acute three-veined lemma. Montana describes lemma ~2–4 mm, awnless or awn-tipped. Distinguish a glume point or awnlet from a true long lemma awn. Measure several mature one-flowered spikelets, detach and photograph each glume and dorsal lemma with a 1-mm ruler; no organ-level arrows are justified from the present wide photographs.
field_id_short_tiles.status: PUBLISHED MEASUREMENTS — NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO MEASURED SPIKELET DISSECTION

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 05 · CENTRAL TEXAS LOOK-ALIKES — DO NOT IDENTIFY BY A WIRE HEAD ALONE
field_id_short_tiles.short: Sideoats grama has many short pendent side branches; tumblegrass has fewer long, rigid, widely diverging racemes on a curved axis.
field_id_short_tiles.details: Lindheimer muhly has a denser upright flowering panicle; nimblewill has a small narrow contracted panicle; purple lovegrass produces a diffuse airy cloud. Tumblegrass requires its distinctive whole branching pattern plus mature spikelet attachments, true ligule and one-flowered anatomy. Do not infer a species from an old detached tumbling seedhead or a close-up of one branch alone.
field_id_short_tiles.status: SOURCE-BASED LOOK-ALIKE LESSON — MATCHED COMPARISON PHOTOS PENDING

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 06 · PUBLIC-READY GATE — PHOTO AND SITE HANDOFFS
field_id_short_tiles.short: FIELD_READY_PHOTO_GAPS: three existing archived source photographs, three species teaching panels; fine anatomy remains unverified.
field_id_short_tiles.details: NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO (Grass Photo-Finish): a vouchered rooted Central Texas tuft plus complete curved head; two opposite faces of ONE attached raceme with 1-mm scale to document actual spikelet orientation; true ~1–4 mm membranous ligule on same specimen; mature dissected 3–6 mm spikelet with both glumes and three-veined lemma, awn tips resolved. NEEDS_SITE_QA (Public Learner Readiness): verify all three archived JPEGs, per-photo CC BY-NC/CC BY-SA 2.0 rights, EXIF/GPS removal, original two gross arrows, correct scientific synonym, six tile rendering, and rights-filtered public gallery. No new images, arrows, genus/family edits or Pages actions. Do not claim 100% until scientific orientation discrepancy and anatomical pixels are resolved.
